text:
jonathan: Quick alert — noticed a regression surface when FlashAttention2 + paged KV are both enabled on SM90 (CUDA 12.1). Baseline on SM80 (CUDA 11.x) looks fine, but on SM90 p95 latency jumps and throughput drops. Need sleuth help. :eyes:

sasha: Can you drop numbers and a short repro?

jonathan: Short repro = small seq (64/128) + paged_kv=true + batcher enabled. Microbench run (same model shard, same batcher config):

```
SM80 (CUDA 11.8, custom CUDA fused): throughput ~11.2k tok/s, p95 ~82ms
SM90 (CUDA 12.1, Triton kernels default -> Flash2 variant): throughput ~8.4k tok/s, p95 ~138ms
Paged KV disabled on SM90 -> throughput back to ~11.0k tok/s, p95 ~88ms
```

jonathan: So paged KV + Flash2 on SM90 only. Not seeing this on large seqs (>512).

kevin: Interesting. Do you have nsight/nsys flame or kernel counters?

jonathan: Pasted the narrowed nsys snippet (trimmed):

```
[nsys summary]
Kernel: flash_attn_fused_v2    time 43.2ms   L2_read 9.8GB   sm_eff 0.42
Kernel: flash_attn_fused_v1    time 21.1ms   L2_read 3.1GB   sm_eff 0.79
(page loads appear more frequent; L2 traffic ~3x)
```

cheng: That smells like cache thrash / different memory access pattern for paged KV that triggers a different memory-bound code path on SM90. SM90 has different L1/L2 behavior and larger warps/changed scheduling -> some tiling/packing assumptions in Flash2 might be invalid.

kevin: Another angle: Triton-generated kernels sometimes change vectorization/gradual fallback for sm>=90. We added a more generic path for boundary conditions to be safe. That codepath could be using smaller shared memory per CTA and so more global loads.

jonathan: Kernel selector currently picks flash2_tuned if (arch >= 90 && cuda_version >= 12.0 && model.type == 'gpt'). That heuristic is too coarse given paged_kv.

sasha: Quick mitigation options: 1) add paged_kv-aware selector to prefer "flash1_fused" for short seqs, 2) force sm80-compat fallback on SM90 for paged_kv until we root cause, 3) tweak batching heuristics to avoid creating many small micro-batches at tail.

kevin: For (3) what's the current tail behavior? We coalesce batches with max_delay=12ms but small tail ratio still ends up with many sub-32 token batches when requests are sparse. That increases kernel launches and reduces occupancy on SM90.

jonathan: Right — on SM90 the same micro-batch pattern leads Triton to generate many small grid launches and the flash2 path doesn't scale down well.

perf-bot: Quick run recommended: tools/bench.sh --arch sm90 --kernels flash2,flash1 --paged-kv true --seq 64,128 --batch 1..16. I've queued this on dedicated perf pool.

cheng: Also check register/spill counts for the two kernels. If flash2 uses more registers per thread on sm90 it can reduce occupancy drastically.

jonathan: I grabbed a ptxas log: flash2 uses ~100 regs/thread on sm90 triple-warp config vs 56 regs/thread on sm80 build. That matches the occupancy drop.

sasha: OK actionable plan:
- kevin: add a conservative selector rule: if paged_kv=true and seq <= 128, prefer "flash1_fused" on any arch until we have perf tests. (short PR)
- jonathan: instrument microbench to log L2 traffic + reg usage per-run and attach to canary runs. (today)
- cheng: run nsys full traces for a small sample and check shared mem / bank conflicts. (tomorrow)
- ops-bot: schedule canary on 5% of sm90 instances with selector change.

kevin: I'll open the PR now with a flag so we can A/B. If results look good we can backfill more aggressive heuristics.

ops-bot: Canary scheduled: group=sm90-canary-5pct start=now end=2h. Rolling configs will apply to ~120 instances.

jonathan: If the quick selector patch regains ~95% of throughput, we can avoid emergency rollback. Otherwise revert.

sasha: Also add a perf regression alert tied to kv_paged=true + arch=sm90 so we get notified next time.

kevin: PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime@refs/heads/pagedkv-selector-1799 (link). Patch adds condition and unit tests for sequence thresholds.

jonathan: Running the perf-bot bench now; will report numbers in ~15m. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: bench results (first pass):

```
sm90 flash2 paged_kv seq=64 batch=8 -> 8.5k tok/s p95 140ms
sm90 flash1 paged_kv seq=64 batch=8 -> 10.9k tok/s p95 90ms
sm80 flash2 paged_kv seq=64 batch=8 -> 11.3k tok/s p95 84ms
```

jonathan: Looks like selector patch will work. I'll follow up with nsight captures for the accepted canary runs.

cheng: Filing follow-up ticket to audit Triton codegen for tile sizes on sm90 and verify register pressure heuristics for flash2.

kevin: Nice find. Long term we should: 1) add per-arch microbench harness, 2) extend kernel selector to consider (paged_kv, seq_distribution, batch_tail_ratio, cuda_version).

sasha: Agreed. Low-risk immediate fix + medium-term selector improvements. Closing loop after canary completes. :white_check_mark:
